judgment.notes: A001 instantiates M002 with real field, X=V×R, target W, U, point (x,r), order 2. These are normed real spaces; H002 supplies all coordinate derivatives, and BG001-BG003/BG008-BG009 verify C^2 at this point using only a positive-time neighborhood. The minimum order is 2 as stated in M002. BG010-BG011 identify the two evaluations with the claimed coordinate partials. A002/A003 use M001 in the real algebra R on each identical pair of scalar component curves, with derivatives (u_tt)_k and, using F002, (u_jt)_k respectively; BG012 verifies the zero extension at r>0. A004 uses the scalar curves s↦(u_t)_k(x+(s-x_j)e_j,r) and s↦(u_j)_k(x+(s-x_j)e_j,r) at s=x_j, with derivatives (u_jt)_k and (u_jj)_k by H002 and D007/D006. All three product-rule premises are met in each application; BG013 justifies adding the derivatives.

S001 correctly takes derivative maps from H002 and forms smooth component products and finite sums; BG004-BG007 verify these routine closure steps, including converting the squared norm to the component square sum without differentiating the norm at zero. S002 applies the given symmetry theorem to the locally smooth total extension and obtains ∂r u_j=u_jt, rather than taking commutation as a definition. S003 differentiates every scalar product using M001, sums by BG013, and substitutes F002; finite real commutativity yields the factors 2 and B_j=u_j·u_jt=u_jt·u_j. This proves both displayed derivative identities with their actual signs and constants. BG014-BG015 verify all asserted joint continuity. Zero component dimension gives empty sums, and zero spatial dimension leaves e's independent smoothness argument valid while spatial-indexed assertions are vacuous. No property at time zero is asserted.
